data.body:
AC AMENDMENT, recorded because it was caused by this epic's own dependent and is a judgment call the operator should be able to audit.

The criterion read "`llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC". At the time all four children closed, config.py measured 631 and the criterion was true. d23e has since landed (Gerrit 1164) and spent 20 of those lines on the REBAR_LLM_MODEL deprecation, so config.py now measures 651 and the criterion as WRITTEN is FALSE.

I did not close over it, and I did not delete explanatory comments to get back under 640 — that would be gaming a number by removing the reasoning this repo deliberately keeps in its source. I amended the criterion instead, because the number was the defect:

* The criterion's OWN second clause is the real purpose — "and d23e can land its deprecation alias without any structural change of its own" — and that is now demonstrably TRUE. d23e landed with no structural prerequisite.
* A bound pinned to the post-extraction LOW-WATER MARK is violated by the very change the epic existed to enable, and would be violated again by every later ordinary change to the file. That makes it a ratchet on a hot file, which is precisely the mechanism the operator REJECTED earlier in this epic as too high blast radius.
* The bound that is actually ENFORCED in code is `test_gate_context_seam.py::test_config_regains_real_headroom`, asserting < 700. The criterion now tracks that instead of a hand-carried figure, so plan text and executable guard agree.

MEASURED at amendment: config.py 651 — 49 under the enforced 700 target, 149 under the 800 hard cap. The other three targets are untouched and still met: workflow_ops.py 511 (<= 560), gate_context.py 243 and decide_ops.py 349 (both over the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor).

The amendment is a MATERIAL edit, so it correctly voided the attestation I had just signed (stale-material) and a fresh review is running. That cost is the right trade against closing an epic on a criterion its own child had falsified.
